2022_09_5_d_transmittal_letter_for_fy23_.page:
**Document.** Transmittal letter dated March 28, 2022 from Dr. Wanda Cook-Robinson, Superintendent, Oakland Schools, addressed "Dear Board of Education Designate," forwarding the proposed Oakland Schools budget for FY 2022-23. Copies to District Superintendent and District Business Manager.

**Statutory basis and vote.** Per the Michigan School Code, Section 380.624(2), the proposed FY 2022-23 General Fund budget goes to constituent districts' Boards of Education for review by May 1, and not later than June 1 each constituent board shall adopt a resolution of support or non-support. Budgets for all funds were included for transparency, but LEA Designates vote only on the General Fund budget.

**Revenue outlook.** Oakland Schools is primarily funded by property tax dollars; the budget projects a growth factor in property tax revenues of 4.0%. Projections are called conservative against Oakland County taxable value increase projections because a Headlee rollback of the operating millage is considered probable for FY 2022-23 -- triggered when annual growth on existing property exceeds inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index. Taxable values and the millage reduction factor arrive by June 1.

**Major budget features.**
- Mental health: two mental health consultants added, broadening support of mental health workers in schools under Section 31n of the Revised School Aid Act, plus Youth Mental Health First Aid and Trauma-Informed Instruction.
- Career and Technical Education: aligned to the Michigan Department of Education's Top 10 in 10 Years goals; four technical campuses, career program redesign, and operational funding for the CTE mobile classroom (the STEMi), operational in spring 2021. The CTE allocation to LEAs rose more than 25% in 2019-20 and that level continues in 2022-23.
- Cybersecurity: multi-factor authentication, an endpoint detection and response platform for local districts, and phishing simulation exercises.
- Shared services on a cost recovery basis: technology to sixteen constituent districts, business office services to four districts through an intergovernmental agreement (IGA), plus instruction and truancy services.
- MiPEER: formed in FY 2012-13 by Oakland Schools and 22 Oakland County school districts as the Michigan Partnership for Essential Education Resources; members convert to PowerSchool BusinessPlus in phases between 2015-16 and 2022-23.
- Illuminate Education has been the countywide student assessment vendor since Fall 2016, covering twenty-eight (28) districts and two (2) public school academies; the Board agreed to a 50% subsidy for 2022-23, with "Item Banks" add-ons at districts' cost.
- Countywide communications channel: $700,000 in the 2022-23 General Education Fund budget to connect districts to first responders via an emergency radio channel.

**Personnel costs.** Step increases plus a 2% across-the-board salary increase, subject to collective bargaining. Eight state-mandated retirement rates are in effect; the most common choice, Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy, is projected to remain at 28.23% for 2022-23, against an overall blended rate of 28.26%.

**PA 152 health care hard cap** (medical price index growth projected at 3.7%):

| Tier | Plan year beginning after 1/1/22 | Plan year beginning after 1/1/23* |
|---|---|---|
| Family | $19,921.45 | $20,658.54 |
| Individual plus one | $15,276.01 | $15,841.22 |
| Single | $7,304.51 | $7,574.78 |

*projected, assuming growth in the Medical CPI of 3.7%

**PA-18 special education.** Property tax revenue growth of 4.0% is projected. The base distribution of PA-18 funding to local school districts is budgeted to increase approximately $7.9 million or 5.6%; another $2.7 million covers group home expenditures, reimbursements for educating incarcerated youth, special education program startup, extraordinary expenditures and capital. In FY 2021-22, Oakland Schools distributed additional PA-18 funds totaling $5.4 million above the base distribution.

**Planning and calendar.** A five-year forecast is updated with each budget amendment using Oakland County Equalization taxable value projections; a five-year capital plan is updated annually with at least three and up to five years pre-funded. Budget presentation to the 28 local district business managers at the Oakland County School Business Officials meeting April 22, 2022; Designates Meeting April 25 at 6:00 PM in Conference Room C; resolutions due on or before June 1, 2022; Truth in Budgeting hearing and approval consideration June 7. Questions to 248.209.2424.
2022_09_5_d_transmittal_letter_for_fy23_.verbose:
Oakland Schools Superintendent Dr. Wanda Cook-Robinson issued this transmittal letter on March 28, 2022, addressed "Dear Board of Education Designate," inviting constituent district boards to review the enclosed proposed Oakland Schools budget for FY 2022-23. The Oakland Schools Board of Education and the Superintendent jointly extend the invitation. The letter closes with copies to the District Superintendent and the District Business Manager, and directs budget questions to the Superintendent's office at 248.209.2424, promising prompt replies. Page markers ii, iii and iv appear in the extracted text.

STATUTORY FRAMEWORK AND THE CONSTITUENT VOTE. Per the Michigan School Code, Section 380.624(2), the proposed FY 2022-23 General Fund budget is to be submitted to its constituent districts' Boards of Education for review by May 1. Not later than June 1, the board of each constituent district shall adopt a resolution of support or non-support of the General Fund budget. For transparency purposes, Oakland Schools included the budgets for all of its funds in the enclosed document; however, it is only the General Fund budget upon which constituent districts vote, and the letter repeats that while Oakland Schools provides all of its fund budgets for review, LEA Designates are only voting on the General Fund budget.

PROPERTY TAX REVENUE AND HEADLEE. Oakland Schools is primarily funded by property tax dollars. The budget projects a growth factor in Oakland Schools' property tax revenues of 4.0%. Tax revenue projections are characterized as conservative compared to Oakland County taxable value increase projections because there is concern that a Headlee rollback of the operating millage is probable for FY 2022-23. The letter explains the mechanism: a rollback occurs when the annual growth on existing property is greater than the rate of inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index. Additional information regarding taxable values and the millage reduction factor will be received by June 1.

SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL WELLBEING AND MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT. Oakland Schools has always provided resources in the areas of social-emotional wellbeing and mental health support, and the pandemic increased the need for these services substantially. To meet those needs, resources were shifted toward mental health support by adding two mental health consultants. These positions will broaden the support of mental health workers in schools under Section 31n of the Revised School Aid Act. Support for professional learning will deepen in programs such as Youth Mental Health First Aid and Trauma-Informed Instruction.

CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION. To align with the Michigan Department of Education's Top 10 in 10 Years goals and strategies, additional resources are dedicated to career and technical education. Beyond significant resources for the four technical campuses, the 2022-23 budget includes additional funds for career program redesign and operational funding for the CTE mobile classroom -- the STEMi -- which was operational in spring 2021, bringing STEM activities to local districts. In 2019-20 the CTE allocation to LEAs was increased by more than 25%, and that level of funding continues in 2022-23, providing local districts additional resources for local CTE programs from elementary to high school.

FOCUS ON CYBERSECURITY. To maintain the safety, security and integrity of applications and data managed by Oakland Schools, significant investments are being made in cybersecurity. Activities include increasing the use of multi-factor authentication, implementing an endpoint detection and response platform for local districts to detect and thwart security threats, and conducting cybersecurity awareness and phishing simulation exercises. Significant supports are available to constituent districts for cybersecurity awareness and evaluation.

SHARED SERVICES. Oakland Schools provides services to Oakland County districts above and beyond its normal service model, including technology, business office, instruction and truancy services provided on a cost recovery basis. Technology services are currently provided to sixteen constituent districts, and business office services are currently provided on a limited basis to four districts through an intergovernmental agreement (IGA) with Oakland Schools.

MiPEER CONSORTIUM. In FY 2012-13, Oakland Schools and 22 Oakland County school districts formed the Michigan Partnership for Essential Education Resources (MIPEER) to select a countywide Enterprise Resource Planning system for human resource and financial applications. Since then the Consortium has standardized the Chart of Accounts and created many best practice business processes for each function -- finance, human resources, budgeting and procurement. Consortium members are converting to the PowerSchool BusinessPlus software in phases between 2015-16 and 2022-23.

ILLUMINATE. Oakland Schools has contracted with Illuminate Education as its countywide student assessment and data analysis tool vendor since the Fall of 2016, and all twenty-eight (28) districts and two (2) public school academies are included in the software license and support agreement. Illuminate DnA provides teachers with one place to build and administer formative assessments, capture and analyze multiple sources of data to inform instruction, and direct students to learning resources supporting specific, targeted standards. The Oakland Schools Board of Education agreed to provide a 50% subsidy for the student assessment software and support in 2022-23; additional add-ons called "Item Banks" can be purchased through the contract at the districts' cost.

SUBSIDIES. The Illuminate DnA subsidy is one of several. Oakland Schools provides multiple software products at no cost or reduced cost to constituent districts in the areas of Career and Technical Education and curriculum and assessment. A subsidy is provided on the per pupil cost of the PowerSchool BusinessPlus system for districts that are members of the MiPEER consortium. Communication tools such as news services and media monitoring/clipping services are provided to LEAs at no cost. These subsidies in the 2022-23 budget are exclusive of pass-through grant funds, other district allocations, and the cost of dedicated staff who support student and finance/HR software and applications.

COUNTYWIDE COMMUNICATIONS CHANNEL. The 2022-23 General Education Fund budget includes costs for a countywide communications channel in the amount of $700,000. The project is intended to connect constituent districts to first responders via an emergency radio channel.

PERSONNEL COSTS. Step increases for eligible employees are included in the 2022-23 budget along with a 2% across-the-board salary increase. All union salary changes including step adjustments are subject to collective bargaining, and the increase is in accordance with the current bargaining agreement. Regarding the State-mandated retirement rate, there are 8 rates in effect depending on the hire date of employees and their choices for eventual retirement benefits. The most common employee choice is Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy, and that rate is projected to remain at 28.23% for 2022-23. Oakland Schools analyzed its own employee choices and projected an overall blended retirement rate of 28.26% for 2022-23.

HEALTH CARE HARD CAP. The "Hard Cap" for employee health care costs remains in effect for all labor groups. The hard cap dollar limits that employers may pay are subject to annual adjustment based on the medical price index, over which the school district has no jurisdiction. Oakland Schools projected growth in the medical price index of 3.7%. The stated limits are:

| Tier | Plan year beginning after 1/1/22 | Plan year beginning after 1/1/23* |
|---|---|---|
| Family | $19,921.45 | $20,658.54 |
| Individual plus one | $15,276.01 | $15,841.22 |
| Single | $7,304.51 | $7,574.78 |

*projected, assuming growth in the Medical CPI of 3.7%

PA-18 SPECIAL EDUCATION FUNDING. Oakland Schools receives property tax revenue for support of Special Education programs. In FY 2022-23 there is growth projected in property tax revenue of 4.0%. The base distribution of PA-18 funding to local school districts is budgeted to increase approximately $7.9 million or 5.6%. Additionally, $2.7 million is budgeted for other LEA distributions for group home expenditures, reimbursements to districts for educating incarcerated youth, special education program startup and extraordinary expenditures, and capital. In FY 2021-22, Oakland Schools distributed additional PA-18 funds totaling $5.4 million above the base distribution.

PLANNING FOR THE FUTURE. Oakland Schools states it is dedicated to sound financial planning and preparing for future economic uncertainties. It utilizes a five-year forecast that is updated with each budget amendment and incorporates projections from Oakland County Equalization for taxable values. It also maintains a five-year capital plan updated annually to prepare for necessary improvements and upgrades to facilities and equipment, and the organization pre-funds at least three years and up to five years of the capital plan requirements. The letter pledges continued work to ensure the budget reflects commitment to increasing student achievement, using economies of scale to decrease operating costs for local districts, customizing and regionalizing programs and services for diverse constituent district needs, and assisting schools and districts in meeting state and federal mandates.

APPROVAL CALENDAR. A presentation of the budget to the 28 local school district business managers was scheduled at their meeting of the Oakland County School Business Officials on April 22, 2022. The Oakland Schools Board of Education would then hold a Designates Meeting on April 25 at 6:00 PM in Conference Room C, giving local board designates and district administration an opportunity to review the General Fund budget before submitting their board's resolution to Oakland Schools on or before June 1, 2022. The Oakland Schools Board of Education will hold a Truth in Budgeting hearing on June 7 and will consider the FY 2022-23 proposed budget documents for approval during its regular meeting that night.
